- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.3), model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture mean reversion or rebound.
- Model shows strong bias toward “mean reversion” in 30-day horizon — if recent 18-day average is >72, forecast often settles below; adjust downward if sentiment is weak.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00), model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5 units in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling (e.g., sentiment 1.00, price dropping), model may overcorrect; reduce forecast slope or add slight downward bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is consistently above true outcome by >2%, consider sentiment-driven mean reversion rule: subtract 0.5–1.0% per 3-day lag if sentiment is low.
